title: I Found the Perfect First Business for Introverts
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: No paid promotion is disclosed; the interview promotes the guest's services and personal brand.

stated_problem.quote: founders that are very much in the business and understand the power of AI, yet their teams are not really implementing it the way that they could be.
stated_problem.speaker: Ryan Shooter

idea.name: AI implementation and advisory for businesses
idea.one_liner: Helps founders and business teams adopt AI by advising, teaching, and building tools and workflows; earns through coaching, cohorts, and project fees.
idea.customer: Founders, business owners, and organizational leaders who want better AI adoption, operations, or marketing systems.
idea.offer: Business and AI advisory, private coaching, cohort-based education, and implementation builds such as workflow automation, marketing tools, websites, and content repurposing.
idea.revenue_model: Project fees, monthly private coaching, and per-person cohort fees; some clients continue into implementation projects after a cohort.

key_quotes.quote: founders that are very much in the business and understand the power of AI, yet their teams are not really implementing it the way that they could be.
What the private coaching looks like, usually it's a 3month sort of deep dive into your business.
Give or take it's 5 to 10 grand a month.
The cohort groups are essentially month-long sprints with me where I get groups of the one I'm doing right now, 10 people to build alongside each other a common goal.
I don't know how obsessed I am with the AI agent terminology, but building AI tools that are scheduled and fit directly into your business.
For instance, the most recent one I did was working with the realer to repurpose content and just produce a lot large amount amounts of content for them.
It's been business advisory, how we're implementing AI and the software tools into their company, making sure that they're on track to reaching their goals.

claims.claim: The customer businesses Ryan had worked with ranged up to about $20 million in revenue, usually below $10 million.
claims.quote: up to 20 million is probably the range I've worked with so far, but it it is usually sub 10 million

claims.claim: He planned to hold 100 free calls before considering charging for services.
claims.quote: I told myself I would have 100 free calls with people and then look into charging for some of my services.

claims.claim: He completed 100 conversations after booking more than 100.
claims.quote: All well of the ones that I got booked because I booked way more than hundred and I ended up having the 100 conversations.

claims.claim: He estimated reaching about 150 people before losing track of the free calls.
claims.quote: I probably got to 150 or so when I lost count after 100 cuz I stopped being meticulous about tracking these specific free calls.

claims.claim: He said he contacted three to four times as many people as those who took a call, aiming for 100 conversations.
claims.quote: But I probably hit up three to four times more than people that hopped on the call. So the goal was uh not 100 reachouts but 100 real conversations which takes hundreds of reachouts.

claims.claim: He estimated that 60% of his initial conversations came through business groups, split roughly between local and online groups.
claims.quote: I would say 60% from the business groups I'm loosely associated with. Maybe we could split that half and half with local versus online groups that I met along the way.

claims.claim: The host described the calls as 100 one-hour Google Meet calls.
claims.quote: 100 calls each an hour long on Google Meet.

claims.claim: The host calculated roughly an 8–9% close rate from 150 reachouts and 12 paying customers.
claims.quote: some one time from 150 reachouts. So, eight nine% close rate.

claims.claim: Ryan said he closed one or two early projects for between $500 and $1,000 each.
claims.quote: Yeah, I probably did close one or two on some very low-end projects just to get get the ball rolling. I was charging probably between, you know, $500 and $1,000 for those sort of projects.

claims.claim: He tried mass email outreach and said it produced no results.
claims.quote: Again, I did attempt to do the, you know, mass email outreach. Nothing happened with it.

claims.claim: He had one private coaching client in a three-month sprint.
claims.quote: Right now I'm per client I have one client doing that with me in the current you know 3 month sprint.

claims.claim: He charges $5,000–$10,000 per month for private coaching.
claims.quote: Give or take it's 5 to 10 grand a month.

claims.claim: Private coaching takes about 10 hours per week per client.
claims.quote: Probably takes 10 hours or so a week for me to focus on that.

claims.claim: He wants to take at most one or two high-ticket clients.
claims.quote: I I want to take on one or two of those people max.

claims.claim: His current cohort had 10 participants.
claims.quote: The cohort groups are essentially month-long sprints with me where I get groups of the one I'm doing right now, 10 people to build alongside each other a common goal.

claims.claim: The cohort costs $1,000 per participant.
claims.quote: What do you charge for this? This is just $1,000.

claims.claim: He described the cohort work as roughly 10 hours per week, based on the listed weekly sessions and support.
claims.quote: So, let's say 2 hours on Monday, 2 hours on Thursday, and then 5 hours in between. So, another 10.

claims.claim: He said he could roughly double cohort capacity to 20 people.
claims.quote: Probably double that size. 20 people.

claims.claim: A previous cohort had three participants and brought in $3,000 for the month.
claims.quote: The second one I did, three people still $3,000 a month.

claims.claim: He said implementation builds can range from $1,000 to a possible $15,000–$20,000, depending on the project.
claims.quote: It could be anywhere between $1,000 and I can imagine charging like 15 to $20,000.

claims.claim: He estimated that a typical customer might spend about $2,000 across a cohort and a later project.
claims.quote: Probably I would say the average person joins a cohort group of mine and then probably works on a project with me. So, about $2,000 maybe on average.

claims.claim: He projected his best month to be about $15,000.
claims.quote: I'm going to have the best month of my life, which is about to be making about 15 grand this time projected.

claims.claim: He said about half of current-month clients were new engagements and half were continuing clients.
claims.quote: The month I'm having right now, I probably about have 50% of the people being first engagement clients and then the other half being clients that I've been working with.

claims.claim: He said he reached out to 10 people per day from his contacts.
claims.quote: I reach out to 10 people every day doing the same thing I've been doing for the past year. I go into my contacts and I see what sort of value can I provide.

claims.claim: The host estimated that 350 hours of work produced $1,500 in early revenue, assuming two projects at $750 each.
claims.quote: 350 hours to get your first call it 1500 in revenue. Let's say two people at 750 each.

claims.claim: The host estimated that this early revenue worked out to about $2 per hour.
claims.quote: So, your hourly rate is terrible at this point. You're looking at two bucks an hour for sure.

claims.claim: A prior cohort had one participant.
claims.quote: I called it a I called it a cohort group cuz I tried to get more people to join. I had one person join.

claims.claim: He said one customer paid him about $15,000 over roughly a year of work.
claims.quote: Yeah, I've been working with the same business for the past year or so now. So, I've made about 15 grand working directly with them.

claims.claim: The host stated that Ryan had moved to $10,000–$15,000 per month working for himself, and Ryan affirmed it.
claims.quote: To 10 to $15,000 a month working for yourself. That's right.

claims.claim: Starting the AI implementation business cost about $20.
claims.quote: How much did it cost you to start an AI implementation business in total? $20.

acquisition_channels.details: Warm outreach to personal and professional contacts by text, phone, email, and LinkedIn DM; he said the outreach was not cold.
Local AI and business groups, online masterminds, and networking groups.
YouTube demos, guides, workshops, and social media used to show expertise and provide value.
He said referrals from his personal network contributed to later work.
He tried mass email outreach, which he said produced no results.

ideas.delivery: Ryan conducts discovery and advisory conversations, teaches founders and teams in private coaching or group cohorts, and builds or helps implement AI tools and workflows. Much of the work is delivered through Google Meet and shared screens; he also sometimes meets people in person.

uk_legal_risk.reason: Customer acquisition relies heavily on individual text messages and social DMs to personal contacts. If UK recipients are individuals or sole traders, marketing texts and DMs may require consent or an applicable exception; a warm contact list alone does not establish that.

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to contact lists and CRM data. For email outreach, the transcript's mass-email attempt would need to follow PECR rules, including the corporate-subscriber distinction and opt-out requirements; cold calls should be screened against TPS/CTPS. No subscription or employment-agency service is described.
